results.fact: Trailhead (Cedar Creek vs Silver Star Creek / Hwy 20 pullout)
results.correct_value: The climb starts at the Cedar Creek Trailhead (end of FR 200 / Sandy Butte-Cedar Creek Road, off SR-20 between MP 175 and 176, ~4.25 mi west of Mazama); the Hwy 20 pullout near MP 166 is only where the Burgundy Col descent comes out.
results.evidence: The first-ascent account (NWMJ) has both the 2000 and 2005 parties starting from the Cedar Creek trailhead/parking lot, and Mountain Project's East Ridge page says to approach from the Cedar Creek Trailhead via the old horse packers' trail. The Forest Service and WTA place Cedar Creek TH at the end of FR 200 (Sandy Butte-Cedar Creek Rd), 0.8 mi off SR-20 between MP 175-176, ~4.25 mi west of Mazama and 17-18 mi from Winthrop. The pin sits at the MP 166 pullout (coordinates out of scope), so it is relabelled as the descent finish; USGS 1 m DEM puts that pin at ~4,230 ft, not 5,400.

results.correct_value: V (for the 5.9+ line the row grades); IV applies only to the 5.8 style that skirts sub-summits, as pro_tips already explains
results.evidence: Mountain Project lists the East Ridge as Trad/Alpine Grade V, 5.9+, noting the FA party graded their skirting solo IV 5.8 but that roping up or staying on the crest makes it 5.9+ V or harder. The NWMJ record lists the on-crest East Ridge (Silver Horn) as Grade V, 5.9+ and the 2000 skirting line as IV 5.8. The row's grade/rock_grade are 5.9+, so its commitment is V; alpine_grade IV was the outlier chip.

overview, approach, approach_variants[0] and partner_requirements all give the ridge as about 3.5 miles; the NWMJ first-ascent article says the east ridge stretches over 3.5 miles from the Cedar/Early Winters confluence to the summit. length_m 1609 (exactly 1 mile) is the lone outlier.

4,400 ft is impossible: the Cedar Creek trailhead sits at ~2,985 ft (USGS 1 m DEM at WTA's trailhead coordinate 48.5792,-120.4787; WTA gives Cedar Falls, 500 ft above, as 3,500 ft), so the net rise to the 8,876 ft summit alone is ~5,900 ft before the ridge's many sub-summit ups and downs. No source found states the route's total gain, so no number is written.

results.correct_value: Childs & Goldie, Sept 14 2000, soloed the ridge unroped (no gear placed, no pitch belayed, two short rappels); Beckey & Beckstead's 1986 route was the Northeast Spur joining the upper east ridge, III 5.8
results.evidence: Mountain Project's East Ridge page credits the FA to Geof Childs and Larry Goldie 9/14/2000 and says they soloed the entire ridge. The NWMJ first-person account says they went 14 hours car-to-car without placing gear or belaying a pitch, with two short rappels, and records Beckey/Beckstead (Sept 12, 1986) as the Northeast Spur & East Ridge, Grade III 5.8, approached via Varden Creek; SummitPost and Wikipedia also list the NE Spur & E Ridge as Grade III 5.8. The fa column's 'first continuous roped ascent' and its 'soloed unroped ... Grade IV' for 1986 were both wrong.

results.fact: Water at the Bench and the col
results.correct_value: Waypoints are right: seasonal water at the bench and snowmelt at the col, both until late summer
results.evidence: The Mountaineers route page says water is available at both the bench and Burgundy Col until late summer, and Mountain Project says to grab water at the col. That supports waypoints[2] and waypoints[3]; the conflicting claims (no water at the col; a spring running well into September) are in bivy[0] and bivy[1], which are owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch.

USGS 1 m DEM gives ~4,080 ft at the crossing pin and ~4,315 ft at the pullout; a hiking route description says the trail drops 200 ft to the river, and the route's own approach text says 150-200 ft. 4,450 ft (above the trailhead) is impossible.
